hero.filename: Flag half mast NZ parliament buildings Pike River mining tragedy.jpg
hero.title: File:Flag half mast NZ parliament buildings Pike River mining tragedy.jpg
hero.source: Flag half mast NZ parliament buildings Pike River mining tragedy
hero.description: The flag on New Zealand's Executive Wing of Parliament, known as the 'Beehive', flies at half mast on December 2, 2010 to mark the official memorial service for the 29 miners who died in the Pike River Mine tragedy 13 days earlier. The white marble Parliament House building in the foreground.

gallery.title: File:Stand With Pike campaign occupation on the access road to Pike River Mine October 2016.jpg
gallery.description: In October 2016 Anna Osborne and Sonya Rockhouse led an occupation of the Pike River Mine access road to stop government mine owner Solid Energy from pouring a 30 metre thick "temporay" concrete seal into the mine's entrance.

gallery.title: File:Brunner Mine Historic Site MRD 09.jpg
gallery.description: The coal mine at Brunner on the Grey River, West Coast, was New Zealand's largest. It was the site of New Zealand's largest mine disaster, when 65 men were killed in a mine explosion in 1896. Today it is the site of a restored heritage area, and has memorials to the victims of the explosion and to the Pike River disaster.
